process_area.title: Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification

value_stream.name: Auto-ID, Barcode, RFID, Price-Tag Labeling & EAS Operations

fields.Trigger: New SKU onboarding (VS-01.1); GS1 standard update; audit finding
fields.Volume: 35,000 active SKUs + ~5–8% annual new SKUs (~1,500–2,500/yr, the corpus canon)

workflows.name: GS1 Membership, GTIN/Barcode Standard & Item-Identification Policy

Automation Opportunity: - New-SKU GTIN auto-suggestion from GPC range; duplicate/reuse detector at item-master save; GS1 Data Hub sync
Controls: - CTL-683 (ensure controlled execution — Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification (PA-151.1).)
- CTL-683: GTIN uniquely assigned & never reused (VS-29); GS1-standard adherence audited; private-label items gated (VS-41)
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 (master data/W1345), VS-137 (PIM), VS-41 (private label), VS-31 (quality), VS-92 (kit GTIN), W4482 (data model)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Duplicate/reused-GTIN risk**: Two SKUs share a code → scan picks wrong item, revenue/Inventory error; mitigated by one-time-assignment rule + duplicate guard
- **Standard-drift risk**: Non-GS1 codes sneak in (vendor/private); mitigated by onboarding validation gate
System Touchpoints: - Item master / GTIN field (VS-29/W1345); PIM (VS-137); private-label items (VS-41); quality (VS-31)
Time Estimate: - ~15 min/SKU onboarding validation; ~1 week annual policy review

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead maintains BuildRight's GS1 Philippines membership, Global Company Prefix (GPC), and the GTIN-assignment rule (GTIN-13/EAN for trade items, GTIN-14 for cases/pallets, GS1-128 for logistics)
Auto-ID Lead assigns/validates GTIN per new SKU, governs reuse (never reuse a retired GTIN) and bundle/kit GTINs (links to VS-92), and publishes to the item master (VS-29)
Auto-ID Lead documents the item-identification policy, trains merchandising/private-label (VS-41), and audits adherence via exception reports (VS-29/W1345)

workflows.name: Item Auto-ID Data Model (GTIN, Serial, Lot/Batch, Expiry, Variable-Measure)

Automation Opportunity: - Attribute-driven barcode-format auto-selection; lot/serial mandatory-flag from item category; catch-weight format validator
Controls: - CTL-683: lot/serial mandatory on regulated/DG items (VS-89/VS-114); catch-weight format validated; recall-traceability verified
Cross-references: - links to VS-29 (attributes), VS-04 (lot/serial receipt), VS-08 (catch-weight POS), VS-89 (recall), VS-114 (DG/SDS), VS-115 (scale calibration), W4481 (GTIN)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Traceability-gap risk**: Lot/serial not captured → recall cannot scope affected stock (VS-89); mitigated by mandatory lot/serial on regulated/DG items
- **Catch-weight error risk**: Wrong variable-measure format → wrong price at POS (links to VS-118); mitigated by validated format & W115 scale calibration
System Touchpoints: - Item master attributes (VS-29); lot/serial capture (VS-04); catch-weight POS (VS-08); recall trace (VS-89); DG/SDS (VS-114)
Time Estimate: - ~20 min/SKU modeling; bulk for category batches

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead defines which attributes ride on the identifier — serial (power tools, appliances), lot/batch (paint/chemical, cement), expiry (limited), and variable-measure (catch-weight lumber/wire/nails) per item type (profile §6.4)

Auto-ID Lead maps the data model to GS1-128 application identifiers and 2D (GS1 DataMatrix / QR) for dense data (lot+expiry+serial), and to the catch-weight/random-weight barcode format (links to VS-08/W115)
Quality/Recall confirm the model supports recall traceability (VS-89) and DG/SDS access (VS-114); DC confirms lot/serial capture at receipt (VS-04)

fields.Trigger: New label need; artwork refresh; RA 7394/DTI change
fields.Volume: Label format set across hang-tag, shelf-edge, adhesive, bulk-yard, variable

workflows.name: Label & Price-Tag Format Specification and Artwork Standards

Automation Opportunity: - Template-driven label auto-layout from PIM data; mandatory-field validator; fixture-aware format selection
Controls: - CTL-683 (ensure controlled execution — Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification (PA-151.1).)
- CTL-683: label carries mandatory fields (price/unit/barcode, RA 7394; PS/ICC VS-117; DG pictogram VS-114); template version-controlled; conformance audited (W4486)
Cross-references: - links to VS-137 (PIM), VS-01.2 (pricing), VS-14 (brand), VS-117 (PS/ICC), VS-85 (mandatory discount), VS-114 (DG/SDS), VS-55 (fixtures), W4486 (conformance)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-compliant-label risk**: Missing PS/ICC mark, price, or DG pictogram → Consumer Act/DTI exposure; mitigated by mandatory-field template + conformance audit (W4486)
- **Format-mismatch risk**: Shelf-edge label doesn't fit fixture; mitigated by fixture-aware format spec (links to VS-55)
System Touchpoints: - PIM/template library (VS-137); pricing (VS-01.2); marketing brand (VS-14); DTI-BPS mark (VS-117); mandatory discount (VS-85); DG/SDS (VS-114)
Time Estimate: - ~3–5 days initial format set; ~2 days annual refresh

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/Merchandising specify the label format set (hang-tag, shelf-edge label, adhesive price sticker, bulk-yard tag, variable/catch-weight label) per item type/channel, with required content fields (description, price, unit, barcode, promo, mandatory-discount notice VS-85)
Auto-ID Lead/Marketing set artwork/brand standards (logo, color, font legibility, bilingual EN/Filipino, DG/SDS pictograms VS-114, DTI-BPS PS/ICC mark VS-117) and the template library in PIM (VS-137)
Auto-ID Lead/PIM govern template version control, publish to stores/DC, and audit format conformance (W4486)

fields.Trigger: Loss/Shrink review (VS-23); RFID program; new high-value category
fields.Volume: EAS/RFID tagging policy across the 35K-SKU assortment

Automation Opportunity: - Shrink-value-driven tagging auto-recommendation; tag-ROI analytics; RFID-encoding automation
Controls: - CTL-683 (ensure controlled execution — Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification (PA-151.1).)
- CTL-683: tagging policy shrink/value-based (VS-23); RFID encoding standard; source-tag agreements (W4498)
Cross-references: - links to VS-23 (LP/shrink), VS-05/VS-60 (inventory visibility), VS-29 (tagging flag), VS-04 (source-tag receiving), W4498 (source-tagging), W4503 (analytics)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Under-protection risk**: High-shrink SKU untagged → avoidable shrink; mitigated by shrink-driven tagging tier
- **Over-tagging cost risk**: Tagging low-value C-items erodes margin; mitigated by value/shrink ROI threshold
System Touchpoints: - LP/shrink analytics (VS-23); inventory visibility (VS-05/VS-60); item master tagging flag (VS-29); DC source-tag receiving (VS-04)

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/LP set which SKUs carry EAS (hard tag, soft label, benefit-denial ink) by shrink/value tier (top high-value: power tools, appliances, PPE, small electronics) aligned to VS-23 shrink targets
Auto-ID Lead/LP set the RFID-tagging policy (RFID-enabled categories for cycle-count/smart-shelf/real-time inventory — links to VS-05/VS-60), tag type (passive UHF), and encoding standard
LP/Auto-ID Lead tune the policy on shrink data (VS-23/W840), evaluate source-tagging with vendors (W4498), and measure tag/loss ROI

fields.Trigger: Hardware refresh; new store (VS-37); RFID program
fields.Volume: 600 POS scanners + store/DC label printers + EAS gates + RFID readers across 205 sites

Automation Opportunity: - Device-fleet/health dashboard; read-failure-by-device analytics; auto-refresh trigger on failure-rate
Controls: - CTL-683 (ensure controlled execution — Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification (PA-151.1).)
- CTL-683: hardware standard certified (VS-99); firmware consistent; read/print performance validated (W4486)
Cross-references: - links to VS-99 (ITAM lifecycle), VS-27.1 (service desk), VS-34 (procurement), VS-07/VS-04 (deployment), W4486 (read/print standard)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Heterogeneity risk**: Mixed vendor/firmware → inconsistent reads & support burden; mitigated by certified-standard & firmware policy
- **Aging-fleet risk**: Worn printheads/scanners → read failures; mitigated by refresh cycle & PM (VS-99)
System Touchpoints: - IT/ITAM fleet (VS-99); service desk (VS-27.1); procurement (VS-34); store/DC deployment (VS-07/VS-04)
Time Estimate: - ~3–4 weeks standard cycle; ongoing fleet mgmt

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/IT set the hardware standard (1D/2D scanner, mobile RF scanner, label printer DPI/media, EAS gate/deactivator, handheld/fixed RFID reader) and certify vendors via Procurement (VS-34)
IT/ITAM manage the device fleet lifecycle (procurement, deployment, maintenance, refresh, secure retirement) via VS-99, and ensure firmware/print-driver consistency across 205 sites
Auto-ID Lead/IT validate read/print performance against the W4486 standard and feed hardware issues to the service desk (VS-27.1)

fields.Volume: Read-rate/conformance across 134.4M annual POS line scans

Automation Opportunity: - Scan-fail-rate dashboard by item/POS; auto-reprint trigger on threshold; image-based label-conformance check
Controls: - CTL-683 (ensure controlled execution — Auto-ID Standards, GS1 Governance & Label/Tag Specification (PA-151.1).)
- CTL-683: barcode-grade gate (ISO 15416); read-rate target > 99.5%; RA 7394 price-tag presence audited (W4487)
Cross-references: - links to VS-08 (POS scan), VS-04 (DC receive), VS-118 (revenue assurance), VS-31 (quality), W4483 (format), W4487 (RA 7394)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Scan-fail risk**: Poor-grade barcode → cashier manual entry/keying error & queue friction (links to VS-118); mitigated by grade gate + reprint
- **Missing-price-tag risk**: RA 7394 violation per SKU/store; mitigated by conformance audit & reprint SLA
System Touchpoints: - POS scan-fail/exception (VS-08); DC receive exception (VS-04); revenue assurance (VS-118); quality (VS-31)

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/Quality define the barcode-quality grade (ISO/IEC 15416 print quality, GS1 minimum grade), the label-conformance checklist (W4483 fields), and the target read-rate (> 99.5% first-pass scan)
Auto-ID Lead/IT monitor scan-fail/manual-entry rates per POS/DC (links to VS-08 exception, VS-04 receive), and flag failing barcodes/labels for reprint
Auto-ID Lead/Quality run periodic label-conformance audits in stores (RA 7394 price-tag presence/accuracy), trigger reprints/corrections, and report to Revenue Assurance (VS-118)

fields.Trigger: Regulation change; new regulated SKU; DTI audit
fields.Volume: Regulatory labeling across regulated categories (~44% DTI-BPS, ~8–10% DG, energy-labeled appliances)

workflows.name: Regulatory Labeling Compliance (RA 7394 Price Tag, DTI-BPS, DG/SDS, Energy Label)

Automation Opportunity: - Regulatory-matrix-driven label-field validation; missing-label exception report; DTI-audit evidence pack
Controls: - CTL-683: RA 7394 price tag on every item (audited); DTI-BPS PS/ICC present (VS-117); DG pictogram + SDS (VS-114); energy label (VS-120)
Cross-references: - links to VS-22 (compliance), VS-117 (PS/ICC), VS-114 (DG/SDS), VS-120 (energy label), VS-100.3 (legal), VS-55 (shelf compliance), W4486 (audit)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Consumer-Act violation risk**: Missing/wrong price tag → DTI fine + consumer complaint; mitigated by RA 7394 audit + reprint SLA
- **Regulatory-miss risk**: Missing PS/ICC/energy label → sale prohibition/fine (VS-117/VS-120); mitigated by regulatory matrix gate
System Touchpoints: - Compliance/permits (VS-22); DTI-BPS mark (VS-117); DG/SDS (VS-114); energy (VS-120); legal (VS-100.3); shelf compliance (VS-55)

steps.activity: Compliance/Auto-ID Lead maintain the regulatory labeling matrix: RA 7394 price tag (every item, every store), DTI-BPS PS/ICC mark (VS-117), DG hazard pictogram + SDS access (VS-114), energy-efficiency label (appliances, RA 11285/DOE), age-restricted (solvents/cutting tools)
Compliance/Stores verify labeling at store via W4486 audits and shelf-edge compliance (links to VS-07/VS-55), escalate gaps, and reissue labels
Compliance/Legal manage DTI/consumer-protection audit response (links to VS-22), track violations, and drive corrective action

fields.Trigger: GTIN/format/tag change; price change; promo; system sync

workflows.name: Auto-ID Change Control, Synchronization & Master-Data Handshake

Automation Opportunity: - Change-control workflow with effective-date; automated cross-channel sync verification; drift auto-detection
Controls: - CTL-683: auto-ID changes change-controlled & effective-dated; sync latency monitored (< 30s); cross-channel price/label reconciled (VS-118)
Cross-references: - links to VS-27/VS-113 (IT/EA), VS-29 (master data), VS-01.2/VS-58 (pricing/promo), VS-10 (ecommerce), VS-118 (revenue assurance), W4481–W4483 (spec)
Pain Points / Risks: - **Sync-drift risk**: Price/label mismatch across channels → over/under-charge (links to VS-118); mitigated by near-real-time sync + drift reconciliation
- **Uncontrolled-change risk**: GTIN reuse/format change mid-life → scan chaos; mitigated by change-control + effective-dating
System Touchpoints: - POS↔ERP sync (profile §14.3); PIM (VS-137); WMS (VS-04); pricing/promo (VS-01.2/VS-58); ecommerce (VS-10); EA (VS-113)

steps.activity: Auto-ID Lead/IT govern change control for GTIN/barcode/format/tag data (request, approve, effective-date, rollback) and the POS↔ERP↔PIM↔WMS synchronization (profile §14.3 near-real-time)
Pricing/Promotions push price/promo changes to shelf-edge labels and POS (links to VS-01.2/VS-58), with reprint triggers and effective-time coordination (bi-monthly sale events)
IT/Auto-ID Lead monitor sync health (latency < 30s per profile §15.3), reconcile POS-local cache vs central, and resolve drift before it reaches the customer (links to VS-118)
